analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. I examined both head-text units (lines 416-801 and 802-1210) and the patch excerpt. No code, authorization, crypto or attestation behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant documentation delta: GLM5Next video handling (head lines 810-813, 829). Variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are now described as indexed by presentation order and timed at i / nominalFrameRate, not refused with a 400. Processor refusals remain deterministic 400s, and tower and MLX faults keep the retriable refusal. The documented bounds are unchanged: 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (`maximumDecodedBytes`), 28,532 prepared-pixel visual-token cap, one-video-at-a-time decode, and a `VisionMemoryGate` reservation sized to the worst case. Media requests stay excluded from prefix lookup and capture (`permitsHybridCheckpoint`), so the T-041 cross-tenant prefix-cache/TTFT concerns are not widened.

The patch also adds an 'Inline video labels' bullet near head line 1896 (`MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders`: mp4, x-m4v, quicktime, mov). The excerpt is truncated and that line is outside the supplied text units, so the sentence ('The label only gates the p…') can't be assessed.

Remaining integration questions, all in code not supplied here: (1) whether the GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset change that accepts VFR video still enforces the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap and the 600 s / 384 Mpx request limits before frame decode, since the VFR path can have a different frame count or duration relationship than the constant-frame-rate path; (2) whether `nominalFrameRate` of zero or NaN is handled; (3) the truncated label-gating text. These are unverified code contracts, not evidence of a regression, so no finding is raised.

The other examined text (Nemotron Super slot, calibration, prefix cache bridge ordering) reads as pre-existing description. I identified no new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions in it.
